2026-05-01.text:
Spent the morning touring Hearst Castle's Neptune Pool and Casa Grande, then drove up the coast to watch elephant seals and pelicans at Piedras Blancas under bright midday sun.

**Highlights:**
- [Hearst Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Castle) — Built 1919–1947 for William Randolph Hearst; designed by architect Julia Morgan in Spanish Colonial Revival style
- [Neptune Pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neptune_Pool) — Outdoor marble pool featuring a Greco-Roman temple façade; completed in its current form in 1936
- [Piedras Blancas elephant seal rookery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedras_Blancas) — Major northern elephant seal haul-out site near San Simeon, open for free public viewing year-round
- [Brown pelican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_pelican) — Pacific Coast species; once endangered, recovered after DDT ban in 1972

2026-05-02.text:
Spent the evening at Sensorio in Paso Robles, moving through Bruce Munro's glowing fiber-optic landscape after sunset and into full darkness. The installation transformed the oak-studded Central Coast hills into an otherworldly illuminated meadow.

**Highlights:**

- [Sensorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensorio) — outdoor art experience in Paso Robles opened in 2019, set across 15 acres of Central Coast wine country terrain
- [Field of Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_of_Light) — solar-powered installation by British artist Bruce Munro featuring approximately 58,800 fiber-optic stems topped with frosted glass spheres; originally debuted at Uluru, Australia in 2016

2026-05-03.text:
Spent early afternoon at Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, taking in McWay Falls from the coastal overlook trail under hazy midday light. The turquoise cove and dramatic cliffs made for a quintessential Big Sur afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [McWay Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McWay_Falls) — an 80-foot tideline waterfall that drops directly onto a secluded beach, one of the few such falls in California accessible by a short trail
- [Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Pfeiffer_Burns_State_Park) — established 1962, named after a pioneering Big Sur homesteader; encompasses roughly 3,762 acres of rugged coastline and redwood canyons
